questions.prompt: What is the purpose of a declaration file?
options: It describes the types of existing JavaScript APIs without providing their runtime implementation.
It replaces the runtime JavaScript implementation.
It proves a package is secure.
questions.answer_key: It describes the types of existing JavaScript APIs without providing their runtime implementation.
questions.explanation: Declaration files describe APIs and should be tested against real consumers and supported versions.

questions.prompt: Which statement is correct about “Understanding Declaration Files”?
options: The concept should be demonstrated with the role of .d.ts and checked against its intended contract.
The safest approach is to skip diagnostics and trust the first output.
A type assertion automatically validates every value at runtime.
The learner should publish hidden solutions so the exercise can grade itself.
questions.answer_key: The concept should be demonstrated with the role of .d.ts and checked against its intended contract.
questions.explanation: The supplied syllabus explicitly includes “The role of .d.ts”; connect it to a concrete example and verify the behavior relevant to this lesson.

questions.prompt: What is a good verification step after practicing “Understanding Declaration Files”?
options: Assume type definitions without implementation code is unnecessary because the code has type annotations.
Ignore compiler or test failures if the interface looks correct.
Treat passing a static token check as proof that the program executed correctly.
Check ambient declarations, include a meaningful failure case where appropriate, and document any runtime or version assumptions.
questions.answer_key: Check ambient declarations, include a meaningful failure case where appropriate, and document any runtime or version assumptions.
questions.explanation: The syllabus includes “Ambient declarations”. Verification should match the concept: type-level checks, runtime tests, configuration checks or human review as appropriate.
